fact: EcoMatin reports the public-contracts minister told the National Assembly finance committee that Coleps, the Cameroon Online E-Procurement System launched in 2018, published 2,334 tender notices in 2025.

The minister said Coleps now has modules for online contract signing and tracking of physical and financial execution, and an arrete of 24 December 2024 sets a calendar for exclusive electronic procurement, with generalisation to all public institutions planned for 2026.
The minister reported 1,173 contracts awarded through Coleps in 2025 from 2,334 notices published, against 365 awards from 458 notices in 2024.

Minister Ibrahim Talba Malla said Cameroon's online e-procurement system COLEPS, piloted from 2019, is in use, with a nationwide stakeholder training campaign launched on 10 October 2024 and awards given to ministries for using it.
The Minister Delegate for Public Contracts says the COLEPS platform, whose second version was launched on 25 June 2025, handles tender notices and online bid submission for public contracts.

The Cameroon Tribune says COLEPS runs the whole public contracts process from tender notice to monitoring of contract execution, and a 27 December 2024 ministerial order makes exclusive electronic award compulsory from the 2027 financial year, regional and local authorities included.

Cameroon Tribune reports that the Minister of Public Contracts's communique of 7 April 2025 requires certain contracting authorities to pass all their contracts electronically through the Coleps platform, under an order of 27 December 2024 setting the migration calendar.
More than 8,143 public contracts worth 1,745 billion FCFA were programmed and published on Coleps for 2025 by January 2025, against 7,372 in 2024, the article says.
